intent: My grandmother's stovetop pressure cooker outlived three of my nonstick pots, and now that mine died I want to buy the kind of thing my own kids might inherit. The stocked options seem to be hard-anodized aluminum or stainless-looking ones at very different prices, and I can't tell which construction actually survives decades of weekly beans and stews. What tends to fail on these things, gaskets, handles, the metal itself? Do the people who've cooked on one for ten-plus years favor a particular build? Give me the one you'd trust to still be working in 2046.
